statement: The Cascajal Block's status is genuinely disputed. It was recovered out of stratified archaeological context (found in a debris pile by road workers), and its proposed c. 900 BCE date rests on associated pottery/figurine dating, not direct dating of the stone. David Grove (University of Florida) reportedly described it as looking "like a fake"; Christopher Pool (University of Kentucky) expressed skepticism in 2010, citing the unusual horizontal sign orientation relative to other Mesoamerican scripts and unusually crisp incision-line weathering. Countervailing material-science analysis (Englehardt et al., Ancient Mesoamerica 31(2), 2020) using polynomial texture mapping, XRF, and SEM concluded the material and manufacture are consistent with genuine Formative-period Olmec production — supporting but not resolving the stratigraphic-context problem.
scholarly_disagreement: Named skeptics (Grove, Pool) dispute authenticity/context; Englehardt et al. 2020 material analysis supports genuine manufacture without resolving the out-of-context recovery problem.
